title: 1973 AHSME Problem 4
statement: Two congruent \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangles are placed so that they overlap partly and their hypotenuses coincide. If the hypotenuse of each triangle is \(12,\) the area common to both triangles is

solutions.text:
Put the common hypotenuse from \(A=(0,0)\) to \(B=(12,0).\) The two triangles have their third vertices at \((9,3\sqrt3)\) and \((3,3\sqrt3).\) Their common region is the triangle with base \(AB\) and apex where \(y=\frac{x}{\sqrt3}\) and \(y=\frac{12-x}{\sqrt3}\) meet. This occurs at \(x=6,\) with height \(2\sqrt3.\) Hence the common area is \[ \frac12(12)(2\sqrt3)=12\sqrt3. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
